credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is compiling a functional picture of a specific facility from remote sources. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate reason to research the facility was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — public-records queries, imagery review, and social-media collection against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — profiling activity observed across weeks to months, not a single search session.
Material evidence — saved facility dossiers, exported tenant directories, annotated imagery, or organized notes on occupancy and staffing recovered from the actor.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who observed the actor compiling site details and can describe what was collected, when, and how.
Behavioral specificity — collection concentrated on the named facility, its tenants, and its operating rhythm rather than a general category of building.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained reporter or system log through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip, reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — vague awareness that the actor 'looked up' a building that could fit any prospective visitor.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time lookup with no follow-through or accumulation.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (dispute with the facility, tenant rivalry, litigation).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the research admits a benign reading (prospective tenant, vendor, job applicant, journalist) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that details may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's remote collection shows operational discipline — anonymized research, systematic aggregation of dispersed public data into a usable occupancy and staffing picture, and the literacy to convert directories and imagery into an operational understanding of the site. Capability falls with careless or trivial lookups, reliance on a single shallow source, and collection that never assembles into a coherent picture.
high_signal_anchors: Covert research tradecraft — anonymized searches, use of cut-outs or borrowed accounts, no attributable query trail back to the actor.
Systematic aggregation — dispersed public data (directory, permits, event calendar, imagery, staff posts) fused into a single coherent picture of the facility's function and rhythm.
Occupancy-model construction — the actor reconstructs occupancy cycles, delivery and service windows, and staffing levels from remote signals rather than casual browsing.
Source breadth and tradecraft — collection spans directories, assessor and permitting portals, imagery services, and social media, cross-checked for currency.
Symbolic-calendar literacy — the actor maps anniversary dates, services, or high-occupancy events to the site's exposure windows.
Demonstrated analytic literacy — the actor reasons productively from collected material about when the facility is most populated or most exposed.
low_signal_anchors: Trivial-lookup posture — a single casual search with no accumulation or organization.
Single-source reliance — all knowledge from one public page; no fusion across sources.
No occupancy inference — data viewed but never assembled into a picture of when the site is occupied.
OSINT-only reach with no synthesis — public data touched but not converted into operational understanding.
Single-modality engagement — only imagery or only a directory; no cross-checking.
Direct-contact attempts — the actor called or emailed facility staff for details, breaching the remote, low-exposure discipline that defines this tactic.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when remote collection progresses from broad interest toward operationally specific detail about the facility's people and rhythm, when the actor retains and organizes what is collected, and when profiling is paired with stated grievance against the place or what it represents. Intent falls with generic interest, lookups that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general interest to operational-detail collection about occupancy, staffing, and timing at the specific facility.
Facility-specific focus — collection concentrates on the named site's tenants, hours, and busy windows rather than a category of building.
Operational specificity in collection — assembling occupancy times, shift changes, delivery windows, event calendars, or after-hours staffing for the site.
Symbolic-date targeting — the actor aligns collection with anniversaries, services, or peak-occupancy dates tied to the facility's meaning.
Retention and organization of the dossier — directories exported, imagery annotated, occupancy notes maintained, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with profiling — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed compiling its operational picture; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-interest behavior — broad curiosity about a building or organization not pinned to its operational rhythm.
One-time lookup without escalation — interest surfaced but no accumulation or narrowing.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — prospective-tenant, employment, vendor, or press relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — material viewed casually but not saved, exported, or organized.
Target ambiguity — several facilities profiled without narrowing to one.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when remote collection yields actionable knowledge of the facility — mastery of its occupancy and access rhythm, awareness of when it is most or least populated, exploited insider or public feeds, and the positional ability to eventually reach the site. Opportunity falls when the public picture is stale or thin, when the facility limits its exposed detail, or when a hardened information posture blocks the actor's known collection methods; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Rich public exposure exploited — tenant directories, real-time occupancy feeds, event calendars, and floor detail are openly available and the actor is harvesting them.

Facility pattern-of-life mastery from remote sources — the actor reliably reconstructs occupancy cycles, delivery and service windows, and low-staffing periods without visiting. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Timing knowledge — the actor knows the facility's peak-occupancy events and its after-hours or skeleton-crew windows from published schedules.
Insider or feed connection being exploited — an employee's social feed, a vendor portal, or a public sensor the actor is actively mining for current site intelligence.
Currency of collection — the profile is built on fresh, actively maintained public sources rather than outdated snapshots.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the facility and can align remote-derived timing knowledge with a feasible approach.
low_signal_anchors: Sparse public footprint — the facility exposes little exploitable detail; occupancy and staffing are not published. Durable signal: sticky unless the exposure grows.
Institutional rule-out of insider or feed access — audits or process actively cleared the leakage path, not merely failed to find it.
Stale collection base — the actor's picture rests on outdated imagery or defunct listings that no longer reflect the site.
Exposure reduced without adaptation — the facility withdrew directories or feeds and the actor did not pivot to another source. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and any physical action requires a major travel investment not yet made.

Information-posture change created barriers — the facility hardened its published detail, changed schedules, or scrubbed feeds, blocking the actor's known collection methods; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble site profiling on the surface — a prospective tenant studying a building's directory and hours looks similar to an actor compiling its occupancy picture; a journalist researching an organization looks similar to reconnaissance. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying interest has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — real-estate professionals, appraisers, developers, vendors, and event planners with legitimate reasons to study a facility's tenants, hours, and capacity; prospective tenants or buyers on due-diligence research.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or regulatory research; licensed private investigators on lawful matters; security professionals conducting authorized open-source exposure assessments of the facility.
Personal or community connection — current and former employees, neighbors, congregants, or patrons looking up hours, events, or staff for legitimate reasons.
Non-threatening attention — journalists, historians, and hobbyists researching an organization or building for reporting or interest.
Academic and research purpose — students and researchers in urban planning, real estate, or organizational studies compiling public facility data.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with later-phase facility behaviors elsewhere — physical reconnaissance against the profiled site, acquisition of an attack means, observed dry runs, or alignment of collected symbolic dates with an occupancy window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility lookup with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator showing operational-detail collection about the facility's occupancy or staffing sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus systematic remote collection plus retention against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Indicators persisting despite reduced public exposure sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential progression toward physical reconnaissance. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility open-source exposure assessment; elevation triggers exposure-reduction and a briefing to facility security leadership; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture review anticipating on-site reconnaissance; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor conducts sustained open-source collection on an already-chosen facility's function, tenants, and operating hours through public directories, organizational websites, and permitting or assessor portals
Threat actor reconstructs the facility's occupancy cycles, staffing levels, and delivery or service windows from remote sources, building a model of when the site is most populated
Threat actor compiles symbolic-calendar dates tied to the facility — anniversaries, religious services, public events, or high-occupancy gatherings — mapping them to the site's exposure windows
Threat actor aggregates a tenant and organizational profile of the facility from social media and public records — who occupies it, key personnel, and public associations
Threat actor studies satellite and street-level imagery and mapping services to characterize the facility's layout, approaches, and surroundings without visiting the site

countermeasures.measure: Conduct an open-source exposure assessment of the facility — inventory what a remote researcher can learn about its tenants, hours, occupancy, staffing, and events — and reduce exposed detail where legally and operationally feasible
countermeasures.limitations: Much facility information is public by law (permits, assessor records, corporate filings) and cannot be withdrawn; assessment raises the cost of profiling without eliminating it

countermeasures.measure: Establish OSINT monitoring for anomalous interest in the facility across public directories, mapping-service reviews, event pages, and social media referencing the site, its tenants, or its schedule
countermeasures.limitations: Remote collection largely leaves no trace on facility systems; monitoring catches only the fraction of profiling that surfaces publicly or touches facility-controlled properties

countermeasures.measure: Brief staff and tenants on operational-security hygiene for public posting — limit publication of detailed schedules, shift patterns, occupancy counts, and event turnout that let an outsider model the site's rhythm
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on voluntary compliance across tenants and employees; some occupancy and event detail is operationally necessary to publish and cannot be suppressed

countermeasures.measure: Elevate facility posture around symbolic-calendar dates and known high-occupancy events identified as exposure windows, coordinating heightened awareness and access attention for those periods
countermeasures.limitations: Addresses predictable date-driven exposure but not opportunistic timing; over-application across many dates dilutes attention and strains resources

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Site Profiling indicators reported (sustained open-source collection on the facility, reconstruction of its occupancy or staffing rhythm, compilation of symbolic dates, or organized tenant/imagery research)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation, (b) review the digital footprint of any identified actor, (c) run a facility open-source exposure assessment to see what the actor could have collected, (d) brief facility security leadership on occupancy and event exposure. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor identified with apparent means and proximity to the facility, OR profiling followed by physical-reconnaissance or acquisition indicators for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Collection of a subject's own open-source activity has its own limits. Consult counsel before active monitoring; document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Profiling activity concentrates on the facility's symbolic-calendar dates or high-occupancy events without a named individual actor
response_protocols.action: Elevate facility posture for the identified exposure windows: increase awareness and access attention around the dates, brief staff and tenants on reporting and posting hygiene, review what occupancy and event detail is published, and coordinate with local law enforcement on emphasis for those periods. Reassess at each window close.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Profiling resolves to a specific actor, or a specific date-certain concern emerges
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support any resource requests and to defend proportionality.

tactics.field_notes: Site profiling is the quiet, mostly invisible phase — the actor is building a functional picture of a place they have already picked, and almost all of it happens at a keyboard. The tell is not any single lookup but the assembly: hours, tenants, who works there, when deliveries come, when the building is fullest, what dates matter. Modern OSINT makes this cheap and low-exposure, so it rarely touches the facility's own systems and rarely leaves a mark you can catch in the act. The strongest signal is when remote collection pairs with a grievance already fixed on the place, or when it organizes around occupancy and symbolic dates in a way that only makes sense if the goal is to be there when it counts. The defensive leverage is mostly on the exposure side — knowing what a stranger can learn about your rhythm, and deciding how much of it needs to be public.
observed_contexts: actor who compiled a place of worship's service times, congregation size, and holiday calendar from its public website and social feeds before any visit
arson case where the subject reconstructed a clinic's staffing and after-hours schedule from employee posts and review sites
extremist who annotated satellite and street imagery of a corporate campus, mapping entrances and parking from home
[literature: CISA-SOFTTARGETS-2019 / RAND-SOFTTARGETS-2024 pattern — open-source occupancy and schedule collection against soft targets preceding attack planning]

tactics.name: Physical Reconnaissance
tactics.notes: Direct, bodily observation of an already-selected facility by a threat actor physically present at or near the site. Casing visits, on-foot and drive-by observation, ground-level photography and filming, timing of entrances, deliveries, patrols, and shift changes, dwell-and-watch from adjacent vantage points, and hands-on probing of which doors, gates, and access points are open or unlocked. Distinct from Site Profiling (TF0102), which studies an already-chosen facility through remote records and open sources; from Structural & Blueprint Study (TF0104), which reads engineering documents; from Security Posture Assessment (TF0105), which systematically maps the protection system as a system rather than casing the place in general; and from Surveillance Detection (TF0110), where the actor's gaze turns onto the defenders to detect and defeat being watched. In Physical Reconnaissance the gaze is on the facility itself — the actor is present to see the place directly.
tactics.cpn_notes: Ground reconnaissance is increasingly blended with remote collection — an actor cross-checks what was learned from satellite imagery, permitting portals, and street-view against a physical visit, and may capture geotagged photographs or video on a personal device that later surfaces the site, the timing, and the observation vantage.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over repeated visits, and recoverable evidence backing first-hand reports that the actor was physically present observing the site. Credibility falls when the sighting is single-source, when the observed behavior admits an obvious lawful purpose, and when the temporal pattern is a one-time presence rather than a return pattern.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a witnessed casing visit lines up with the actor's prior site research and a stated grievance against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Return-pattern persistence — the actor is observed at or near the site across multiple visits, at varied times, over days to weeks.
Material evidence — recovered ground-level photographs, video, annotated site sketches, or notes on patrol and entrance timing that physically tie the actor to the location.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named observer (guard, employee, neighbor) who saw the actor observing, photographing, or probing and can describe the behavior, vantage, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the observed activity concentrates on security-relevant features (entrances, cameras, patrol routes, unlocked doors) rather than casual sightseeing.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — reported through a formal suspicious-activity channel by a trained observer, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single uncorroborated sighting, observer cannot be re-contacted or lacked a clear view.
Content-specificity weakness — presence noted but the behavior is generic and could fit ordinary passersby, patrons, or delivery traffic.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a one-time presence with no return, dwell, or follow-through.
Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter has a structural reason to over-read the presence (neighbor dispute, tenant rivalry, prior conflict with the individual).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the presence admits a benign reading (customer, tourist, contractor, transit) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that ordinary loitering may be retrofitted into a casing narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when on-site observation shows operational discipline — covert vantage selection, concealed capture, varied approach, and attention to the facility's security-relevant features rather than its facade. Capability falls with conspicuous loitering, open photography of entrances, and behavior that staff immediately flag as out of place.
high_signal_anchors: Covert observation tradecraft — the actor watches from concealed or plausibly-incidental vantage points, uses a vehicle or a legend, and avoids a fixed observable return pattern.
Concealed capture — photography or video taken discreetly (phone at hip, body-worn, from inside a vehicle) rather than openly aimed at entrances and cameras.
Multi-visit coordination — ground observation is timed to sample different occupancy and patrol windows, showing deliberate sampling rather than a single look.
Attention to defensive features — the actor's observed focus falls on camera coverage, patrol timing, entrance control, and standoff, indicating a trained eye.
Counter-observation behaviors — the actor varies approach and egress, checks whether they are being watched, and adjusts after any staff attention.
Access probing without alarm — the actor tests doors, gates, or unattended entrances in a way that reads as incidental and does not trigger a challenge.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — obvious loitering, standing to photograph entrances in the open, lingering well past any plausible purpose.
No-concealment repetition — repeated visible presence at the site with no cover, vehicle, or attempt at concealment.
Pretext failure on contact — staff immediately recognized the presence as unusual and the actor had no ready explanation.
Untimed single look — one undirected walk-past with no sampling of occupancy or patrol windows.
Feature-blind observation — attention falls on the building's appearance, not on access, cameras, patrols, or standoff.
Challenge-triggering probing — door or gate testing that immediately drew a guard or staff response, showing no operational discipline.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when on-site observation progresses from a casual look toward operationally specific attention — timing patrols, probing entrances, sketching or photographing access points — and when it is retained or paired with a stated grievance against the place. Intent falls with undirected presence, encounters that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose for being there.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general presence toward timing, probing, and capture of specific access and occupancy detail.
Security-relevant focus — observation concentrates on entrances, exits, patrol routes, camera arcs, and unlocked or unattended access rather than the site generally.
Operational specificity in observation — the actor times shift changes, delivery windows, or patrol intervals, or physically tests which doors and gates are open.
Sustained attention to defender posture — the actor returns to observe how security operates over time and adapts approach accordingly.
Retention of collected product — site photographs archived, video kept, timing notes or a hand sketch maintained, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with presence — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or what it represents AND is observed casing it; the pairing is intent-diagnostic in a way neither signal is alone.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-presence behavior — being in the area or admiring the building, not directed at access, timing, or defensive features.
One-time encounter without escalation — presence surfaced but no return, dwell, probing, or capture followed.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — customer, employee, contractor, delivery, transit, or press relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — a phone photo taken casually and not saved, organized, or acted on.
Target ambiguity — the actor loiters near several sites without concentrating observation on this one.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can convert on-site observation into action — mastery of the facility's occupancy and patrol rhythm, first-hand knowledge of unlocked or unmonitored access, geographic proximity that permits repeat casing, and a vantage that reveals when the place is soft. Opportunity falls with defensive friction the actor does not adapt to, distance not closed, or a hardened posture that denies useful observation; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No defensive friction encountered — casing continues unimpeded; the actor observes, photographs, and probes without being challenged.

Facility pattern-of-life mastery — from direct observation the actor reliably knows occupancy cycles, delivery and service windows, patrol intervals, and low-staffing periods. The informational dimension of opportunity.
First-hand access knowledge — the actor has personally found unlocked doors, unmonitored entrances, camera blind spots, or standoff weaknesses by testing them on site.
Usable vantage secured — a concealed or incidental observation position gives repeatable, low-risk eyes on the site's soft windows.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives, works, or routinely transits near the facility and is present during its vulnerable windows.
Direct site access — the actor can enter or approach unsupervised through a legitimate-appearing role, converting observation into reach.
low_signal_anchors: Approach defeated by hardened posture — visible security, active challenges, or surveillance detection blocked useful observation. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Institutional rule-out of access — an access audit or process actively cleared the openings the actor might have found, not merely failed to look.
Structural proximity degradation — the actor's routine reason to be near the site ended (role, residence, contract, transit route changed).
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — the actor left after being challenged and did not return or vary approach. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and repeat casing requires a travel investment not yet made.
Posture change created barriers — randomized patrols, sealed access, or added cameras deny the actor's prior vantage and timing; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Much lawful activity resembles physical reconnaissance on the surface — a photographer framing a building, a delivery driver waiting, a prospective tenant walking the perimeter, or a transit rider dwelling nearby all look similar to casing. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the presence has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — architects, contractors, appraisers, inspectors, surveyors, insurance adjusters, and real-estate professionals with site-visit business; delivery, utility, and service personnel on their routes.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement activity with proper basis; licensed investigators on lawful matters; security professionals conducting authorized vulnerability assessments or penetration tests of the facility.
Personal or community connection — current and former employees, neighbors, congregants, patrons, and passersby with legitimate familiarity or routine presence.
Non-threatening attention — architecture and history photographers, tourists, film and news crews, and hobbyists with lawful interest in the structure.
Ordinary dwell — transit riders, rideshare pickups, smokers, and people waiting or resting near the site with no directed interest in its access or security.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the observation, breadth across modalities, and persistence across repeat visits. A single low-credibility sighting with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility observation with operational specificity — timing patrols, probing entrances, concealed capture of access detail — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus prior research plus a witnessed casing visit against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Observation persisting despite implemented countermeasures, or active access probing, sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority sightings correlating temporally or by vantage may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging, CCTV retention, and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility-vulnerability assessment focused on the observed access; elevation triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the site's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor conducts one or more casing visits to a specific facility, observing on foot or by drive-by without a legitimate purpose for being present
Threat actor photographs or films the facility from the ground — entrances, exits, cameras, barriers, or approach routes — beyond ordinary tourist or hobbyist framing

Threat actor times the facility's rhythm from a dwell-and-watch vantage — entrances, deliveries, shift changes, patrol intervals, and occupancy peaks — recording when the site is crowded or lightly staffed
Threat actor physically probes access — testing which doors, gates, or service entrances are unlocked or unattended, checking fence lines, and trying handles or badge readers
Threat actor walks or drives the approach and egress routes around the facility, noting standoff distance, cover, choke points, and parking near the site

countermeasures.measure: Run a suspicious-activity reporting program with staff and guards trained to recognize and report casing behaviors — repeat presence, timing observation, photography of security features, and door or gate probing — backed by CCTV review for recurring individuals and vehicles
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff attentiveness and reporting discipline; skilled actors observe from concealed vantage or vehicles and blend into legitimate foot and delivery traffic, and much casing is legally protected until it pairs with access probing

countermeasures.measure: Apply CPTED to deny concealed observation vantage — clear sightlines, manage landscaping and adjacent cover, control approach and standoff, and light entrances and perimeter so ground-level watching and probing are exposed
countermeasures.limitations: Fixed environmental changes cannot remove public vantage points across the street or from adjacent property; raises the cost and exposure of observation without eliminating it, and drive-by observation defeats most sightline controls

countermeasures.measure: Randomize guard patrol timing and routes and vary observable security routines so an actor watching from a dwell vantage cannot reliably learn the facility's patrol and shift rhythm
countermeasures.limitations: Randomization raises the observation burden but cannot fully mask fixed events like opening hours, deliveries, and occupancy peaks; effectiveness decays if patrols settle back into a predictable pattern

countermeasures.measure: Harden and monitor access points against probing — secure and alarm service and side entrances, audit locking discipline, log badge-reader and door-forced events, and flag repeat presence via license-plate and loitering detection
countermeasures.limitations: Access instrumentation catches probing at controlled points but not observation from public ground; alarm and log review depend on staffing and tuning, and gentle handle-testing may not register as a forced-door event

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Physical Reconnaissance indicators reported (a casing visit, ground-level photography of security features, observed timing of patrols or occupancy, or a witnessed presence with security-relevant focus)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) preserve and review CCTV covering the observation window and vantage, (b) corroborate the sighting and attempt to identify the individual and any vehicle, (c) check the reported behavior against known legitimate activity (deliveries, contractors, patrons), (d) assess the facility's exposure at the observed access points and brief security leadership. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor returns for a repeat casing visit, is observed probing access, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Photography and observation from public space are frequently lawful; base any action on articulable behavior, not presence alone. Identification and monitoring of an individual may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active monitoring and document the investigative basis.

response_protocols.trigger: Pattern of repeat casing at the site, active access probing (door, gate, or badge-reader testing), or dwell-and-watch timing observation across multiple visits
response_protocols.action: Elevate facility posture: increase and randomize visible security presence, secure and alarm the probed access points, brief staff on the specific behavior and reporting path, retain and centralize CCTV, and coordinate with local law enforcement on a field interview or patrol emphasis. Reassess at a defined interval.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probing succeeds in gaining or testing entry, the actor aligns observation with an occupancy or anniversary window, or staging-class behaviors surface elsewhere for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes and access hardening are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Coordinate any law-enforcement field contact on articulable suspicious activity, not presence alone.

tactics.field_notes: Physical reconnaissance is where a plan first touches the ground, and it is the most catchable phase because the actor has to be present to see the place. The tells are behavioral, not demographic: someone timing the door instead of using it, photographing the camera instead of the building, walking the fence line, or trying a handle that a customer would never touch. The single strongest discriminator is repetition — one look is a passerby, the same person back at different hours studying the same access is casing. The hard part is that most of this happens from public space where observation is lawful, so the reporting bar is articulable behavior and return pattern, not presence. Access probing is the line where casing stops being passive: when the gaze turns into trying doors, treat it as advancing, not horizon.
observed_contexts: actor conducting repeat drive-by observation of a clinic at shift-change times, later found with phone video of the entrance and staff-parking area
arson case in which the actor walked the rear service alley of the target twice before the attack, testing which delivery door was left unlocked after hours
guard suspicious-activity report of an individual photographing camera placements and timing the patrol loop from a bench across the street over several days
[literature: SANDIA-GARCIA-VAPPS-2006 / DHS-ISC-RMP-2021 pattern — ground reconnaissance and access probing preceding forced or covert entry against a defined facility]

tactics.name: Structural & Blueprint Study
tactics.notes: Acquisition and study of the engineered fabric of a specific facility — floor plans, architectural and engineering drawings, building permits, structural details (load-bearing walls, columns, progressive-collapse points), utility risers, HVAC pathways, and fire-suppression schematics — to reason about where the structure breaks. Distinct from Site Profiling (which studies the facility's function, tenants, and occupancy) and from Physical Reconnaissance (on-site observation of the place), this tactic concerns the actor acquiring information about the physical structure itself: how it is built, how it fails, and which points yield the greatest effect. It is also distinct from Security Posture Assessment (the guards-and-cameras system) and Capability Acquisition (obtaining physical tools and materiel); here the object acquired is knowledge of the building's engineering, not the security overlay or the means of attack.
tactics.cpn_notes: Structural study is increasingly enabled by online sources — municipal permitting portals, FOIA-released drawings, assessor and code-enforcement records, contractor bid packages, and BIM or CAD files exposed on the sites of architects and engineers — that reveal a facility's structural fabric before any restricted document is sought.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor has acquired and studied structural documentation of a specific facility. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate interest in the building's engineering was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — grievance against the place, document-acquisition activity, and technical inquiry about the structure observed against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — sustained pursuit of the building's drawings and structural detail across weeks to months, not a single records request.
Material evidence — recovered floor plans, permit files, annotated blueprints, marked-up risers, or saved engineering drawings that physically tie the actor to the named site.

First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who saw the actor obtain or study the facility's plans and describe structural weak points; high-resolution reporting of the content, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor sought drawings of the specific facility, address, or wing rather than generic architectural material.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained records custodian, contractor, or reporter through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip that the actor 'was asking about the building's plans,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — vague interest in the building's construction that could fit any renovation or curiosity.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time records request with no follow-through or technical follow-up.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (permitting dispute, contractor rivalry, litigation over the building).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the actor's interest in the drawings admits a benign reading (prospective buyer, contractor, code student) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that details of what was requested may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's pursuit of structural information shows operational discipline and engineering literacy — covert acquisition of non-public drawings, use of cut-outs and pretexts, and the ability to read plans productively for load paths, standoff, and collapse mechanics. Capability falls with conspicuous requests, public-records-only reach, and an inability to interpret what is acquired.
high_signal_anchors: Covert acquisition tradecraft — anonymized records requests, cut-outs, or insider elicitation that avoids attaching the actor's identity to the facility's drawings.

Restricted-material acquisition — the actor obtains non-public engineering documents such as structural drawings, fire-suppression schematics, utility risers, or as-built plans not available through public portals.
Multi-modal coordination — permit-portal research, contractor or insider elicitation, and physical confirmation of structural features coordinated across overlapping timeframes.
Pretext durability — cover stories for wanting the building's plans (prospective tenant, contractor, researcher) hold up under records-custodian or facility scrutiny.

Demonstrated engineering literacy — the actor reads acquired drawings productively, reasoning correctly about load-bearing elements, columns, progressive-collapse points, standoff, or utility and fire-system chokepoints.
Document-handling discipline — acquired plans are organized, annotated, and retained in a manner consistent with operational planning rather than idle curiosity.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — openly demanding sensitive drawings from front-desk staff, lingering over restricted plan sets in the open.
Public-records-only reach — all structural knowledge is from permitting portals and assessor records; no operational reach to non-public engineering material.
Pretext failure on initial contact — records staff or contractors immediately recognized the request as unusual.
Interpretive failure — the actor obtained drawings but cannot read them, asking questions that reveal no structural understanding.
Single-modality engagement — only a records pull or only a verbal inquiry; no coordination across sources.
Direct-contact attempts — the actor sought direct engagement with facility engineering or management for plans, breaching operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the actor's engagement with the building's engineering progresses from general drawings toward the specific detail of how the structure fails, when acquired plans are retained, and when structural study is paired with stated grievance against the place. Intent falls with generic construction interest, requests that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general floor plans to acquisition of load-path, column, standoff, or collapse-relevant detail about the specific facility.

Failure-point focus — attention concentrates on what breaks the structure: load-bearing walls, transfer columns, progressive-collapse mechanics, utility risers, or fire-suppression defeat, not on layout for its own sake.

Operational specificity in inquiry or document selection — asking about structural standoff, column spacing, riser locations, or fire-system controls; selecting structural and mechanical sheets over cosmetic plans.
Sustained study of the engineered fabric — the actor works through the drawings over time, cross-referencing sheets and confirming features rather than glancing once.
Retention of acquired materials — plans saved, permits archived, schematics annotated with weak points, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with structural study — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed acquiring or studying its structural documentation; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-construction interest — broad curiosity about architecture or building methods, not pinned to how a specific structure fails.
One-time records request without escalation — a plan set obtained but no technical follow-through or pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — prospective-buyer, contractor, code-compliance, or academic relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — drawings viewed casually but not saved, organized, or annotated.
Target ambiguity — plans for multiple buildings gathered without narrowing to one facility as the objective.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can act on structural knowledge of the facility — combining accurate understanding of its load paths and collapse points, access to the drawings that reveal them, exploited insider or contractor channels, and the positional ability to reach the vulnerable elements. Opportunity falls with restricted-document controls not defeated, insider channels closed, or a hardened structure whose weak points are not exposed; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No acquisition friction encountered — the actor obtains the facility's structural documentation unimpeded despite records controls.

Structural weak-point mastery — the actor reliably knows the building's load-bearing elements, collapse-critical columns, standoff limits, and utility- or fire-system chokepoints. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Restricted-drawing access — the actor holds non-public engineering documents (as-builts, structural sheets, fire-suppression schematics) that expose how the structure fails.

Insider or contractor channel being exploited — an identified engineer, facilities employee, or vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging for drawings or structural detail. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor can reach the structural elements identified in the plans and is positioned to act on that knowledge.
Direct structural access — the actor has unsupervised access to riser rooms, mechanical spaces, or load-bearing areas through a legitimate role.
low_signal_anchors: Acquisition defeated by document controls — need-to-know distribution, watermarking, or portal restrictions actively blocked the actor's access to sensitive drawings. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the controls drop.
Institutional rule-out of insider channel — access audits or process actively cleared the engineering-document exposure, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior document or facility pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation).
Friction encountered without adaptation — the actor abandoned a records request after being challenged and did not return or find another route. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Weak points not exposed — the acquired material is cosmetic or public-portal layout only; the load-path and collapse detail that would create opportunity was never obtained.
Posture change created barriers — drawings pulled from public portals, distribution tightened, or structural hardening implemented; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble structural and blueprint study on the surface — a contractor pulling as-builts looks similar to an actor acquiring collapse detail; a code student reading permits looks similar to reconnaissance. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying interest in the building's engineering has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — architects, structural and MEP engineers, general contractors, code and fire inspectors, appraisers, and insurance adjusters with legitimate need for the facility's drawings; prospective buyers on due-diligence structural review.

Legal authority — authorized building officials, fire marshals, and inspectors exercising code jurisdiction; security professionals conducting authorized vulnerability or blast-standoff assessments of the facility.
Facilities and maintenance work — in-house engineering, renovation, and maintenance staff and their vendors working from as-builts, risers, and fire-suppression schematics as routine business.
Non-threatening attention — building-history and preservation researchers, architecture students, and hobbyists reading permits or plans out of documented interest.
Academic and research purpose — students and researchers in architecture, structural engineering, urban planning, or historic preservation with legitimate document needs.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation — a public permit pulled once — sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity about the structure — acquisition of non-public structural drawings paired with weak-point inquiry — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus document acquisition plus technical study against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Indicators persisting despite implemented document controls sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a structural-vulnerability review of the exposed elements; elevation triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the building's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture and structural-hardening review; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor obtains floor plans, architectural drawings, or building permits for a specific facility through public permitting portals, FOIA requests, or assessor and code-enforcement records

Threat actor acquires non-public engineering documentation — structural drawings, as-builts, load-bearing and column details — through insider elicitation, contractor channels, or theft rather than public sources
Threat actor studies the facility's utility risers, HVAC pathways, and fire-suppression schematics, focusing on service chokepoints and system-defeat rather than layout

Threat actor demonstrates engineering literacy about the structure, reasoning about load-bearing walls, transfer columns, standoff, and progressive-collapse points where the building would fail catastrophically
Threat actor references structural vulnerabilities of a specific facility in communications, describing where the building is weakest or how it could be brought down

countermeasures.measure: Reduce publicly exposed structural detail — remove or redact full drawing sets, structural sheets, and fire-suppression schematics from permitting portals and FOIA releases where legally and operationally feasible
countermeasures.limitations: Much permit and assessor material is public by law and cannot be withdrawn; redaction raises the cost of research without eliminating access to structural information

countermeasures.measure: Monitor permitting-portal access, FOIA requests, and vendor or contractor record requests for the facility's structural and mechanical drawings, flagging repeated or targeted pulls of sensitive sheets
countermeasures.limitations: Requesters may use cut-outs or public terminals; anonymized and third-party requests defeat attribution, and public-portal downloads may leave no reviewable log

countermeasures.measure: Classify and control sensitive engineering documents — enforce need-to-know distribution, watermark drawing sets, and require secure handling and return by contractors and vendors with access to as-builts and structural plans
countermeasures.limitations: Legitimate projects require broad drawing distribution; controls depend on contractor discipline and cannot recover documents already released into circulation

countermeasures.measure: Conduct a structural vulnerability and progressive-collapse assessment of the facility, hardening standoff, load paths, and utility- and fire-system access to reduce the value of acquired drawings to an attacker
countermeasures.limitations: Structural hardening and standoff improvements are capital-intensive and constrained by existing construction; reduces but cannot eliminate exploitable collapse or system-defeat points

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Structural & Blueprint Study indicators reported (records requests for the facility's drawings, study of risers or fire-suppression schematics, references to structural weak points)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation, (b) determine which structural documents were exposed and through what channel, (c) review permitting-portal and records-request logs for the facility, (d) brief facility engineering and security leadership on the structural risk picture. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor identified acquiring non-public engineering documents, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor and records-request auditing may implicate privacy, public-records, and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active monitoring; document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Actor acquires non-public structural documentation or demonstrates engineering literacy about the facility's load paths, standoff, or progressive-collapse points
response_protocols.action: Elevate the case. Convene an engineering-informed vulnerability review of the exposed elements, tighten distribution and monitoring of the affected drawing sets, evaluate interim structural- and system-hardening options, and coordinate with law enforcement given the collapse-relevant nature of the study. Reassess posture on a defined cadence.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Structural study pairs with capability acquisition, dry runs, or a date-certain or occupancy-window signal
response_protocols.legal_notes: Structural-hardening and document-control actions are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Coordinate disclosure of vulnerability findings on a need-to-know basis.

tactics.field_notes: Structural study is the tactic where a plot stops being about a place and starts being about a structure. The tell is not that someone has the floor plan — plenty of legitimate people do — but that the interest runs to where the building fails: the load-bearing walls, the transfer columns, the standoff, the riser and fire-suppression chokepoints. Most of the acquisition is lawful and quiet; permits, assessor records, and contractor bid sets are public or semi-public, and a determined actor can assemble a serviceable picture of a structure without ever touching a restricted document. The signal sharpens when public material is supplemented by non-public engineering drawings pulled through an insider or contractor, and when the actor can actually read them — reasoning correctly about collapse mechanics rather than just collecting sheets. That combination, especially paired with a grievance against the place, is what separates a curious records pull from target development.
observed_contexts: actor who filed successive public-records requests for a government building's permit set and structural sheets, then asked a contractor acquaintance about the load-bearing walls
insider case where an employee copied as-built drawings and fire-suppression schematics for a facility outside any work assignment
arson-and-collapse plot in which the actor studied a building's utility risers to identify where a fire would spread fastest and disable suppression
[literature: FEMA-426-2011 / DOD-UFC4010-2018 pattern — structural standoff and progressive-collapse vulnerabilities as target-development focus preceding facility attacks]

tactics.name: Security Posture Assessment
tactics.notes: Mapping and probing of the targeted facility's physical protection system (PPS) to locate where it fails: camera coverage and blind spots, guard-force size, posture, and patrol timing, access-control type, alarm and lock systems, standoff distance, and response-force timing. Includes deliberate low-level probing — testing a door, attempting a tailgate, inducing a false alarm — to measure detection and reaction. Distinct from Physical Reconnaissance (TF0103), which cases the site itself, and from Structural & Blueprint Study (TF0104), which reads the building's construction. It is also distinct from Surveillance Detection (TF0110): 0110 is the actor defeating observation of the actor, while 0105 catalogs the defenders' system and its gaps. The object here is the protective system's weaknesses, not evading the defenders' gaze.
tactics.cpn_notes: Security-posture assessment is increasingly informed by public and semi-public sources before any physical probe — vendor case studies naming a facility's access-control or camera platform, procurement and bid records exposing alarm and guard-service contracts, installer reviews, and social posts by staff or visitors that reveal patrol routines, badge types, and camera placement.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is cataloging the facility's protective system rather than passing through it. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate interest in the security posture — a vendor, an auditor, a curious patron — was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — probing behavior at the site, questions to staff about security, and saved notes on cameras or guards against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — repeated attention to the facility's countermeasures observed across weeks, not a single pass.
Material evidence — recovered diagrams of camera arcs, annotated guard-patrol timings, or notes on alarm and lock types that physically tie the actor to the named site's PPS.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named guard or employee who observed the actor testing a door, tailgating, or timing a patrol, reported with resolution on the act, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor mapped specific detection gaps (a named blind spot, a shift-change window) rather than expressing vague security curiosity.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained security officer reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous report of someone 'looking at the cameras,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague observation that a person seemed interested in security, fitting many ordinary visitors.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time glance at a camera or door with no follow-through.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (labor dispute, rivalry with a contractor, litigation over the guard service).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the interest in the posture admits a benign reading (security vendor, insurance inspector, new employee) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that a mundane act near an entrance may be retrofitted to a probing narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when engagement with the facility's protective system shows operational discipline — covert observation of coverage and timing, acquisition of non-public security information, durable pretexts for probing, and the technical literacy to read a PPS and reason about its gaps. Capability falls with conspicuous behavior, OSINT-only reach, and probes that fail on first contact.
high_signal_anchors: Covert observation tradecraft — patrol timing and camera arcs recorded from concealment or across varied vantage points, no obvious return pattern.
Multi-modal coordination — physical probing, elicitation of staff, and research into the security vendor coordinated across overlapping timeframes.

Restricted-material acquisition — the actor obtains non-public PPS information such as camera-placement diagrams, guard-post orders, alarm-zone maps, or access-control specifications for the facility.
Pretext durability — cover stories for probing (delivery driver, prospective vendor, lost visitor) survive guard scrutiny during a challenge.
Graduated probing discipline — low-level tests (a rattled door, a brief tailgate, a triggered sensor) staged to measure reaction while preserving deniability and avoiding commitment.
Demonstrated technical literacy — the actor interprets what is observed, distinguishing real detection from deterrent signage and reasoning about response-force timing and blind spots.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — openly staring at cameras, pacing entrances, lingering at a guard post past any plausible purpose.
No-concealment repetition — repeated probing with no pretext or concealment.
Pretext failure on initial contact — a guard immediately recognized the probe as unusual and the actor had no fallback.
OSINT-only reach — all posture knowledge is from public vendor pages or reviews; no operational reach beyond the browser.
Single-modality engagement — only watching or only asking; no coordination across probing methods.
Reaction-provoking clumsiness — the actor triggered alarms or challenges without any apparent measurement objective, breaching operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when engagement with the protective system progresses from broad interest toward gap-specific detail, when the actor retains what is learned, and when probing is paired with stated grievance against the facility or what it represents. Intent falls with generic security curiosity, encounters that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general security interest to gap-specific measurement of the facility's detection and response.
Countermeasure-specific behavior — attention concentrates on where the PPS fails: a specific blind spot, a shift-change gap, an unmonitored door, a slow response window.
Operational specificity in probing or inquiry — testing which doors are alarmed, timing how long a guard takes to respond, asking after-hours coverage or camera recording retention.
Sustained attention to defender posture — the actor tracks the facility's countermeasures over time and adapts probing as posture changes.
Retention of acquired detail — guard timings logged, blind spots mapped, alarm behavior noted and organized, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with probing — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility AND is observed probing its protective system; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-interest behavior — broad curiosity about security in general, not pinned to defeating a specific facility's system.
One-time encounter without escalation — a single door test or camera glance with no follow-through or pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a security-vendor, audit, inspection, or new-employee relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — posture observed casually but not recorded or organized.
Target ambiguity — attention to several sites' security without narrowing to one facility's gaps.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can exploit knowledge of the protective system — combining mastery of patrol and coverage patterns, awareness of detection gaps, exploited insider access to security detail, and the positional ability to reach the site during its weak windows. Opportunity falls with defensive friction not adapted to, distance not closed, or a hardened posture that blocks the actor's known probing; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No defensive friction encountered — probing continues unimpeded; tests go undetected or unaddressed despite the facility's posture.
PPS pattern-of-life mastery — the actor reliably knows patrol timing, shift changes, camera coverage arcs, and the site's low-security periods. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Detection-gap knowledge — the actor knows specific camera blind spots, unalarmed doors, standoff weaknesses, or the true response-force timing for the facility.

Insider connection being exploited — an identified guard, contractor, or security-vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging for post orders, alarm-zone maps, or access. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the facility and is present during the windows its posture is weakest.
Direct facility access — the actor has unsupervised access through a legitimate role, able to test doors and sensors without challenge.
low_signal_anchors: Approach defeated by hardened posture — the facility's countermeasures actively caught and stopped the probing. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared the security-detail exposure, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior access pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation).
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — the actor left after a guard challenge and did not return or adapt the probe. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and probing requires a major travel investment not yet made.
Facility posture change created barriers — randomized patrols, closed blind spots, or new detection blocks the actor's known probing methods; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble security-posture assessment on the surface — a licensed penetration tester probing doors looks similar to an actor measuring reaction; a security-system salesperson studying camera placement looks similar to reconnaissance of the PPS. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying interest has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Authorized security work — licensed vulnerability assessors and penetration testers under contract; security integrators, alarm and camera technicians, and locksmiths on service calls; guard-force supervisors auditing their own posts.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement activity with proper basis; fire marshals and code inspectors checking egress, alarms, and life-safety systems; regulators auditing physical-security compliance.
Verified professional purpose — insurance risk engineers, loss-prevention staff, and corporate security assessing their own or a client's facility with site-visit business.
Personal or community connection — employees and vendors familiar with routine security procedures; visitors who notice a propped door or a camera without intent.
Non-threatening attention — hobbyists and enthusiasts of access-control or CCTV technology, and photographers whose interest in a building incidentally captures its security features.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation — one door glance, one camera photograph — sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity about the facility's detection gaps or response timing sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus probing plus insider elicitation against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Probing that persists despite implemented countermeasures, or that adapts to posture changes, sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection across security incidents; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility-vulnerability assessment; elevation triggers countermeasure activation and PPS hardening appropriate to the probed gaps; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor covertly maps camera coverage and blind spots at the targeted facility — noting field of view, mounting height, recording versus deterrent devices, and unmonitored approaches
Threat actor observes and records the guard force — headcount, armament, posture, and patrol timing — identifying shift changes and low-coverage windows

Threat actor identifies the access-control, alarm, and lock systems in use — badge and reader type, alarm zones, sensor placement, and after-hours recording behavior — through observation, elicitation, or vendor and procurement records

Threat actor measures response-force timing and standoff — clocking how long guards or police take to reach a point, mapping standoff distance and vehicle approach, and timing the interval between a stimulus and a reaction

Threat actor conducts deliberate low-level probing to measure detection and reaction — testing a door, attempting a tailgate, inducing a false alarm, or breaching a boundary to see who responds and how fast

countermeasures.measure: Conduct authorized red-team and vulnerability assessments of the facility's own PPS to find the same camera blind spots, unalarmed doors, patrol gaps, and response-timing weaknesses an actor would probe, and remediate them
countermeasures.limitations: A point-in-time assessment captures the posture as tested; gaps reopen as equipment ages, staffing changes, or procedures drift, so single assessments decay without a recurring cadence

countermeasures.measure: Instrument for probing detection — treat repeated door tests, tailgate attempts, false alarms, and boundary breaches as intelligence events, correlate them across access logs and cameras, and investigate patterns rather than clearing each in isolation
countermeasures.limitations: Low-level probes are individually mundane and easily dismissed as nuisance alarms; correlation depends on retention, disciplined logging, and analysts empowered to connect events across shifts

countermeasures.measure: Randomize and vary the observable posture — patrol routes and timing, shift changes, and response drills — so an actor cannot reliably map coverage windows or response intervals from repeated observation
countermeasures.limitations: Randomization raises the cost of pattern mapping but cannot conceal fixed infrastructure (camera mounts, door hardware, standoff); determined observation over time still recovers averages

countermeasures.measure: Close and layer detection — overlap camera fields to eliminate blind spots, alarm previously unmonitored doors, and add defense-in-depth so no single observed gap defeats the whole system
countermeasures.limitations: Coverage upgrades are capital-intensive and slow to field; new equipment introduces its own configuration gaps and requires trained monitoring to convert detection into response

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Security Posture Assessment indicators reported — observed camera or guard mapping, elicitation about alarms and access control, response-timing measurement, or a low-level probe (door test, tailgate, induced false alarm)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation against access logs and camera footage, (b) review the digital and vendor footprint of any identified actor, (c) assess whether the probed gap is real and remediable, (d) brief facility security leadership and adjust posture over the probed weakness. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probing persists or adapts after a countermeasure change, OR the actor is identified with apparent means and proximity, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Detaining or questioning a suspected prober raises trespass and false-imprisonment exposure; consult counsel and document the investigative basis before action.

response_protocols.trigger: A pattern of repeated low-level probes (recurring door tests, tailgate attempts, or false alarms) against the same facility, with or without a named individual actor
response_protocols.action: Treat the probing pattern as active target development. Correlate the events across shifts and systems, close or alarm the tested gap, randomize the observable posture over the affected window, run a response drill against the measured interval, and coordinate with local law enforcement on suspicious-activity patrol emphasis. Reassess after remediation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probing resolves to a specific actor, or the tested gap aligns with an occupancy or anniversary window
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Preserve access logs and footage of probes as potential evidence per retention policy.

tactics.field_notes: Posture assessment is the tactic where an actor stops studying the place and starts studying its guardians. The tell is not interest in the building but interest in the system that protects it — where the cameras don't reach, when the guard is elsewhere, how long help takes to arrive. Passive mapping (camera arcs, patrol timing) is nearly invisible and looks like waiting; the covert version scores higher precisely because detectability is low. Active probing is louder — a tested door, a tailgate, a tripped sensor — and each probe is individually forgivable as a nuisance, which is exactly why they slip past. The discipline that catches this is treating probes as intelligence: logging them, correlating them across shifts, and asking not 'did we clear it' but 'is someone measuring us.' A single false alarm is noise; a pattern of them against one facility is reconnaissance.
observed_contexts: actor timing guard patrols and photographing camera mounts across several unhurried visits before a planned forced entry
series of after-hours door tests and one induced fire-alarm evacuation, later assessed as response-timing measurement rather than nuisance
insider-adjacent case where a former contractor elicited badge-reader type and alarm-zone layout from current staff
[literature: SANDIA-GARCIA-VAPPS-2006 / DHS-ISC-RMP-2021 pattern — adversary path analysis and PPS gap-mapping preceding facility intrusion]

tactics.name: Capability Acquisition
tactics.notes: Obtaining the physical means to attack a chosen facility — accelerants and ignition sources, explosive precursors or components, breaching and forced-entry tools, a vehicle suitable for ramming, protective equipment, or the funds to procure them. Distinct from Structural & Blueprint Study and Site Profiling (which acquire information about the place) and from Network Development (which assembles the people). The acquisition logic here is about materiel: securing the objects and money that convert a plan against the site into a deliverable method. Because a method reveals itself in what is bought, an incendiary or explosive acquisition against a facility carries more signal than a plan alone.
tactics.cpn_notes: Capability acquisition is increasingly mediated online — marketplaces and hobbyist suppliers, cryptocurrency and stored-value payment rails, and shipping to drop addresses let an actor assemble accelerants, precursors, components, tools, or protective equipment for a facility attack with reduced face-to-face exposure, though purchase and financial records create a durable detection surface.
